_comment: NIST 800-61-aligned response playbooks, one per incident category, keyed by category. The responder selects by incident.category, adapts steps to the investigation, and prioritizes by 'order'. Steps obey the ResponsePlan/PlaybookStep contract: any action containing a destructive marker (isolate/quarantine/disable/block/wipe/delete/reimage/shutdown/kill process/revoke/reset password) sets requires_approval=true, and automatable steps are never destructive.

steps.action: Open an incident ticket and notify the targeted user
Block the sender domain and phishing URL at the mail gateway and proxy
steps.justification: Disrupts mail flow / browsing; analyst must confirm scope.

steps.action: Reset password for the targeted account
Purge delivered copies of the email from all mailboxes
steps.justification: Reversible mail-flow action, safe to automate.

steps.action: Confirm no credential reuse and close the ticket
Open incident ticket and correlate the source IP against authentication logs
Block the offending source IP at the firewall
steps.justification: Perimeter change; analyst must confirm it is not shared infrastructure.

steps.action: Disable the targeted account pending review
steps.justification: Account lockout impacts the user; needs approval.

steps.action: Reset password and enforce MFA for the account
Re-enable the account and monitor for repeat attempts
steps.justification: Judgment call to restore service; not automated.

steps.action: Isolate the affected host from the network
steps.justification: Removes host from network; must be approved.

steps.action: Open incident ticket and snapshot the host for forensics
Kill process and remove the malicious binary
Block the C2 domain and IP at the firewall and DNS
Reimage the host from a known-good image
steps.justification: Wipes the host; explicit approval required.

steps.action: Restore user data and return the host to service
Open incident ticket and quantify the data volume transferred
Block the destination IP and throttle egress for the host
Isolate the source host
Revoke credentials and tokens used in the transfer
Engage DLP and legal review and document the scope
Open incident ticket and map the movement path across hosts
Isolate the compromised hosts along the path
Disable the accounts used for the pivot
Block SMB and RDP between the affected segments
Rotate credentials and restore segmentation
Open incident ticket and log the scanning source
Block the scanning source IP at the perimeter
Review services exposed by the scan and harden them
Confirm no follow-on exploitation and close the ticket
